doc: scipy.ndimage.gaussian_filter(img, sigma, mode=("nearest", "wrap")): truncate 4.0 (radius int(4 sigma + 0.5), taps exp(-x^2 / (2 sigma^2)) normalized to sum 1, computed in float64), axis 0 (rows: "nearest" = clamp at the poles) THEN axis 1 (columns: "wrap" = periodic, folded as many times as the radius needs, also when it exceeds the width), each pass accumulating in float64 and rounding to the input dtype (so a float32 image is rounded to float32 between the two passes); sigma <= 1e-15 returns a copy, a radius that rounds to 0 (sigma < 0.125) is the identity. The 128x64 Earth reference (stored u8, / 255 in float32), sigma 4: a realistic latitude clamp and longitude wrap. Float32 chain: a float64-promoted blur of the same image differs by at most 5.3e-8 (values in 0..1; an independent numpy re-implementation with the same float32 rounding between passes matches scipy bit for bit); the golden float32 tolerance.  Input convention: the u8 input(s) img are maps stored as bytes, and the function receives them as float32(u8) / float32(255) (`u8.astype(np.float32) / 255.0`: the division is done, and correctly rounded, in float32, as measure.load reads an 8-bit map), NOT as the raw bytes and NOT as a float64 quotient (a texel on a histogram edge or a threshold would move). params.u8_inputs lists them.

u8_inputs.img: float32(u8) / float32(255), the division in float32
